methodology: Every pull request that Qwen3.8 27B, an open-weight model, opened on Tau Ceti while running on the AIs@home network, and every task whose attempts have not led to one. Tau Ceti's own review is the judge: a PR is merged only when Tau Ceti merged it. Failed attempts and closed PRs are counted. An attempt is one run of the model on one task; a fix round is a revision pushed after review. A PR's tokens and GPU minutes cover every attempt at its task, failed ones and fix rounds included. GPU hours are the time the model was working, summed over every attempt. Qwen tokens are prompt (including tokens re-read from the cache) plus output tokens. Review rounds quote Tau Ceti's review verbatim. These are our own measurements; PR states as of 2026-10-25.

prs.title: feat: isomorphic number fields have the same class number

changes.reason: The only declaration requires a `K ≃ₐ[ℚ] L` hypothesis when its proof uses only the underlying ring isomorphism, so the public statement is narrower than it needs to be. No duplicate exists in Mathlib or TauCeti.

The main theorem has no docstring because its comment uses `/-!` instead of `/--`, and both comments describe the proof rather than the result. The module docstring also wrongly says no cardinality argument is used and promises a class-group isomorphism that the file never states.
The theorem asks for `K ≃ₐ[ℚ] L` but only uses `e.toRingEquiv`, and both Mathlib lemmas it relies on take a ring equivalence. It should be stated for `K ≃+* L`.

New material has a genuine path to ImaginaryQuadraticClassNumber H1.2 (class-group and class-number transport under Q-algebra isomorphisms), but the description names only the roadmap, not the node. It also exports only the cardinality corollary, which H1.2 explicitly says is not enough.
`RingEquiv.classGroupEquiv` is an unexposed def with no lemma describing it, so consumers cannot relate it to `ClassGroup.mulEquiv` or compute it on ideal classes. Only its cardinality is usable.

`RingEquiv.classGroupEquiv` assumes `NumberField K` and `NumberField L` but never uses them; its ingredients only need `Field K`, `Field L` and the `IsDomain (𝓞 K)` that every field provides. `classNumber_eq` is at the natural level.

`RingEquiv.classGroupEquiv` is the transport the roadmap asks for (§H1.2) and its API is adequate. However, the three new `NumberField.RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv_{refl,symm,trans}` lemmas are general ring-of-integers lemmas exported from the class-number file instead of their existing home, and the refl and symm ones are not tagged `@[simp]`.
